source.title: Evaluating and developing machine learning models — an introduction

questions.question: What does the speaker say must be available before evaluating a model?
key_facts: The evaluation needs the data, model, baseline, optimizer and evaluation setup.

questions.question: Why does the speaker recommend reading papers together with their code repositories?
key_facts: Repositories expose implementation details and possible differences from the paper.

questions.question: What warning does the speaker give about FID implementations?
key_facts: Different implementations can produce non-comparable values.

questions.question: Why does the speaker distrust Python FLOP counters?
key_facts: The counters can omit or miscount operations and should be verified.

questions.question: What information should be recorded for each machine-learning experiment?
key_facts: Record the configuration and the resulting measurements.

questions.question: What advice does she give about positive and negative experiment results?
key_facts: Record and learn from both positive and negative results.

questions.question: Why can a longer context window make time-series prediction worse?
key_facts: Extra context can introduce irrelevant information and degrade prediction.

questions.question: How does she recommend choosing activation functions?
key_facts: Treat activation choice as an experimental design decision rather than assuming one universal best choice.

questions.question: What is the speaker's main process for developing and evaluating a model?
key_facts: Iterate through data, model, baseline, optimization, evaluation and recording.

source.title: So — how does the Internet really work

questions.question: What does the speaker want beginners to take away from the talk?
key_facts: Understand home networks enough to experiment
Reduce fear of computer networks

questions.question: What does a browser receive to display a website?
key_facts: The browser receives the website's HTML source code

questions.question: Why is Internet data split into packets?
key_facts: The network has a bounded message size
Data is divided into small blocks for transmission

questions.question: How does a network switch learn where devices are?
key_facts: It observes the source of devices' first messages and remembers their ports

questions.question: How are wired Ethernet and Wi-Fi related in this explanation?
key_facts: They work similarly at the link-layer level used in the explanation

questions.question: Why do MAC addresses need to be globally unique?
key_facts: Devices on a network need unambiguous lower-level addresses

questions.question: Why does a device need a lower-level address before it can obtain an IP address?
key_facts: It must communicate on the local Ethernet network to request an IP address

questions.question: How can pinging 9.9.9.9 help diagnose a DNS problem?
key_facts: A successful numeric-IP ping shows network connectivity works without name resolution
That isolates DNS as the likely problem

questions.question: What does the speaker discuss after explaining DHCP address assignment?
key_facts: She moves on to DNS and how domain names become IP addresses
